scope: Sparse linear algebra dispatch audit; no claim of a 3x solver speedup or universal SciPy optimality.

environment.source: Worktree Python source with unchanged published a4 native symlink. The upstream manifest distribution metadata says a2 for the reused interpreter, not the source imported through PYTHONPATH.

retained.candidate: Direct ndarray.reshape for exact ndarray LinearOperator callback outputs
retained.reason: The NumPy array-api wrapper delegates to np.reshape, which delegates to this same ndarray method. Preserve reshaped view creation, dtype, shape, strides, ownership/writeability, subclass dispatch, callback order and exceptions. Solver arithmetic remains SciPy.
retained.plain_scipy_comparison: See benchmark/sparse_linalg.json; standard area benchmark records plain-SciPy ratios, not incremental ratios. New regularized Jacobi CG is about 1.67x/1.66x/1.20x at n=32/256/4096; GMRES about 1.16x/1.14x/1.06x.

rejected.candidate: Direct same-dtype CSR/CSC _sparsetools dispatch inside MatrixLinearOperator
rejected.reason: No material improvement beyond direct reshape; added guards erase the Python dispatch savings. One measured GMRES case regressed versus old fastscipy. Would also require additional class/instance override-contract coverage. Not included in production.

rejected.candidate: Replacement CG/GMRES loops or a new SpMV implementation
rejected.reason: Source audit found existing solver arithmetic already uses NumPy/BLAS and SciPy native SpMV. Changing reduction order or iteration policy is outside the exact contract; no numerical-policy exemption or new native kernel proposed.
Prior 2026-10-19 candidate-audit records major-axis/small-block regressions and marginal diagonal wins; not reintroduced.

measurement.method: Median of five repeated timings, 100 calls per solver repeat and 2000 calls per isolated operator repeat. Identical inputs and native=1/BLAS=1 for plain SciPy, pinned old fastscipy, reshape candidate and rejected native candidate. Modes ran in fixed order, so these are exploratory local timings, not cross-platform performance guarantees.
measurement.correctness: Probe compared exact CG/GMRES full results and callback histories against genuinely unpatched SciPy and checked independent equation residuals. No new tolerance or iteration exemptions.

validation.project: 240 passed in tests/test_sparse_linalg.py, including native thread settings 1 and 2.
validation.benchmark: 31 cases byte-identical; all expected fast paths and --check thresholds pass, including two declined controls.
validation.upstream: 1533 outcomes matched in paired test_interface and test_iterative runs; 0 changed outcomes, 0 incomplete pairs, 147502 fast-path calls, 0 fast-path errors. Array API backend skips and existing xfails matched; no quarantine activated.
validation.resources: Probe: 8.46s / 56.0MiB. Validation: 10.57s / 246.4MiB. Each serialized by heavy.lock and tools/platform_suite.run with 512MiB cap and timeout 120s / 180s; native 1/2, BLAS 1; no build.
validation.lint: ruff check and format checks plus git diff --check.
validation.limits: Targeted sparse operator and iterative upstream modules, not all scipy.sparse.linalg. No new architecture test run; implementation is portable Python using the identical NumPy ndarray method.

reproduce: Under the coordination lock/resource monitor, run python bench/runs/2026-10-22-sparse-linalg/probe.py from the repository root. It reconstructs the old implementation from the pinned git commit.

Run python bench/runs/2026-10-22-sparse-linalg/validate.py with PYTHONPATH=python, native threads=2, BLAS threads=1, SCIPY_AVAILABLE_MEM=256Mib, and a process-tree cap. The script executes tests, benchmark, and paired upstream sequentially.
